verdicts.why: In the taste sense it names one of the basic tastes; the sentences are all figurative and do not touch this gloss, and the taste word itself takes no side.
The unpleasantness is the referent (a harsh taste), not an attitude the word adds beyond its meaning.
It states that a thing suits one's purpose; the sarcastic shade in 'so convenient a proposal' comes from the situation, not from the word's default colouring.
Archaic 'large and roomy' is a plain description of size.
A formal synonym of postpone; it says when, not what the speaker thinks of it.
The system of production and consumption is a plain technical noun.
Efficient use of resources is the meaning itself; it is the plain neighbour against which parsimony and stinginess carry the contempt.
An act of economizing is named without approval or scorn.
Making something possible is described neutrally in every sentence.
The faculty of forming mental images is named plainly; any dismissiveness in 'Lydia's imagination' is Austen's context, not the word.
The act of picturing what is not present is descriptive; the word neither praises nor mocks the imaginer.
Resourcefulness is a good quality, but naming a virtue plainly is a positive referent, not a loaded word.
Comparative relation of quantities is a plain measure word.
A part-to-whole quotient is arithmetic, with no attitude.
Magnitude or extent is described, not judged.
Harmonious arrangement of parts is the meaning of this design sense; the word adds no stance beyond it.
Balance among parts is named descriptively.
Feeling sorrow is a plain emotion word; the person is described, not judged.

For the gloss given (things that make you feel sad, as in sad news) the word is descriptive; the 'sad business' sentences belong to the separate deplorable sense, which is not the one under judgement.
Supporting oneself at a minimal level is the meaning, not a sneer; the sentences use the unrelated 'exist between' sense anyway.
A quantity of money is named without attitude.
The result of addition is arithmetic.
The whole amount is a plain quantity word.
A final aggregate is descriptive.
The essential part of an idea ('the sum and substance') is a plain abstraction with no approval or contempt attached.
